+## 4. Decision
+
+Trading OS adopts the following identity model:
+
+```text
+Account.accountId
+    = financial Account identity
+
+BrokerAccount.id
+    = execution/routing identity
+
+Account -> BrokerAccount
+    = explicit durable canonical relation
+```
+
+The two identifiers SHALL remain distinct. Equal UUID values, if they occur by
+accident, SHALL NOT imply identity equivalence.
+
+No service SHALL use any of the following as the canonical relationship:
+
+- equality of the two UUIDs;
+- `(owner, provider)` lookup;
+- display name;
+- provider-specific external identifiers;
+- existence of a risk configuration row.
+
+The exact Java field or persistence representation is an implementation
+decision. The relation semantics are architectural and fixed by this ADR.
+
+## 5. Canonical Relationship Authority
+
+The canonical Account-to-BrokerAccount relation belongs to the account/domain
+model, independently of risk configuration.
+
+The current `account_risk_configuration.broker_account_id` SHALL NOT be the
+sole identity authority because:
+
+- risk configuration may not exist;
+- account identity exists independently of policy;
+- the column currently lacks a foreign key to `broker_account`;
+- PAPER account creation does not create the configuration;
+- risk policy lifecycle must not determine account identity lifecycle.
+
+If the current configuration column remains during migration, it SHALL be one
+of:
+
+- transitional mapping data; or
+- validated configuration metadata that cannot disagree with the canonical
+  Account relation.
+
+It SHALL NOT become a second independently mutable relationship.
+
+Required invariant:
+
+```text
+ACCOUNT_RISK_CONFIGURATION_BROKER_ACCOUNT_ID
+    CANNOT_DRIFT_FROM_CANONICAL_RELATION
+```
+
+## 6. Cardinality
+
+For the first milestone:
+
+```text
+Account 1 <-> 1 BrokerAccount
+```
+
+More precisely:
+
+- one financial Account maps to exactly one BrokerAccount;
+- one BrokerAccount maps to at most one canonical financial Account.
+
+This supports multiple accounts for one user and provider:
+
+```text
+User
+    +-- BrokerAccount A -> Account A
+    +-- BrokerAccount B -> Account B
+    +-- PAPER BrokerAccount -> PAPER Account
+```
+
+The architecture SHALL NOT introduce `BrokerAccount -> N financial Accounts`
+without a demonstrated product requirement for multiple financial views,
+portfolios, or policies over one external account.
+
+This first-milestone constraint remains evolvable through a future ADR.
+
+## 7. Ownership, Provider, and Mode Invariants
+
+### 7.1 Ownership
+
+The linked records must belong to the same authenticated owner:
+
+```text
+Account.user.userId == BrokerAccount.ownerId
+```
+
+Database foreign keys may enforce record existence, but cross-record owner
+consistency requires deterministic domain/application validation unless the
+schema is deliberately designed for composite enforcement.
+
+### 7.2 Provider
+
+`BrokerAccount.provider` is the provider authority.
+
+The legacy `Account.broker` string is metadata and must not become the new
+canonical provider identity. If retained during migration, it must agree with
+the linked BrokerAccount or be treated as stale/legacy data and rejected where
+provider correctness matters.
+
+### 7.3 Execution Mode
+
+Execution mode is authoritative on `BrokerAccount`:
+
+```text
+Account -> BrokerAccount -> executionMode
+```
+
+PAPER is an execution mode, not a `BrokerProvider`.
+
+No duplicate independently mutable execution mode is introduced on `Account`.
+
+## 8. Account Creation Invariant
+
+A newly usable trading account must establish the following logical graph:
+
+```text
+BrokerAccount
+    + financial Account
+    + canonical relation
+    + explicit RiskConfiguration
+    + assigned immutable RiskProfile
+        = risk-ready trading account
+```
+
+For PAPER, the following is insufficient:
+
+```text
+BrokerAccount exists
+    + legacy Rules exists
+```
+
+Account creation must not report a PAPER account as risk-ready unless the
+explicit configuration and profile requirements are satisfied or the account
+is clearly marked unavailable for trading.
+
+The exact local transaction/orchestration boundary remains implementation work.
+
+## 9. Risk Configuration
+
+`RiskConfiguration` represents policy and limits. It is separate from current
+financial state:
+
+```text
+RiskConfiguration
+    = policy, limits, version, assignment and provenance
+
+RiskFacts
+    = current factual account, position and market state
+
+RiskEngine
+    = deterministic interpretation and decision
+```
+
+PAPER SHALL require an explicit, versioned, persisted RiskProfile assignment
+before it is eligible for deterministic trading evaluation.
+
+The legacy `Rules` entity is not implicitly equivalent to the current
+
+- `Rules.java:16-49` is unversioned legacy configuration;
+- `RiskPersistence.java:259-301` models versioned immutable profiles and
+  assignments;
+- `V2__trade_plan_risk_evaluation.sql:1-43` defines the current schema.
+
+The current legacy values are not an authorized default policy for the current
+RiskProfile architecture.
+
+```text
+DEFAULTS_AUTHORIZED_BY_EXISTING_POLICY = NO
+```
+
+The system must not invent a default PAPER profile or silently copy a profile
+from another account. Until an explicit versioned default policy is approved,
+PAPER provisioning must either require explicit setup or remain unavailable for
+trading.
+
+Missing or invalid policy fails closed.
+
+## 10. Risk Facts Boundary
+
+The logical Risk Facts boundary SHALL be neutral and mode-independent:
+
+```text
+RiskFacts boundary
+    +-- LIVE facts
+    +-- PAPER facts
+```
+
+The boundary represents factual snapshots, completeness, timestamps, and
+provenance. It does not evaluate policy or authorize execution.
+
+The existing `BrokerRiskFactsPort` may remain temporarily as a LIVE adapter or
+compatibility boundary. This ADR does not require a mechanical rename. The
+semantic target is a neutral Risk Facts contract, not a naming-only refactor.
+
+## 11. Risk Facts Routing
+
+Risk Facts source selection belongs to Trading Core application orchestration
+or a mode-aware application adapter/router.
+
+The target flow is:
+
+```text
+Application layer
+    -> resolve financial Account
+    -> resolve canonical BrokerAccount
+    -> read execution mode
+    -> select authoritative facts source
+    -> assemble immutable RiskEvaluationContext
+    -> invoke Risk Domain
+```
+
+The Risk Domain SHALL NOT inspect:
+
+- `ExecutionMode`;
+- `BrokerProvider`;
+- repositories;
+- Feign clients;
+- provider DTOs;
+- Broker Service availability.
+
+Mode changes fact acquisition authority, not risk interpretation authority.
+
+## 12. LIVE Risk Facts
+
+LIVE financial and position facts remain externally authoritative where the
+provider owns them:
+
+```text
+LIVE
+    -> Broker Service
+    -> external provider
+    -> provider-neutral Risk Facts
+    -> immutable RiskEvaluationContext
+    -> Risk Domain
+```
+
+Local Trading Core projections may support display, audit, or correlation, but
+must not silently replace fresh provider authority for LIVE risk evaluation.
+
+This preserves ADR-042 and ADR-040 provider reconciliation semantics.
+
+## 13. PAPER Risk Facts
+
+PAPER facts are authoritative in Trading Core:
+
+```text
+PAPER
+    -> persisted Account / AccountBalance
+    -> persisted Trade and execution/fill state
+    -> local baseline and realized state where required
+    -> Market Data for current valuation inputs
+    -> provider-neutral Risk Facts
+```
+
+PAPER risk evaluation SHALL NOT require:
+
+- Broker Service account facts;
+- provider credentials;
+- provider balances;
+- provider position queries;
+- provider reconciliation;
+- external broker mutation.
+
+Market Data supplies current prices and conversion/valuation inputs only. It
+does not own PAPER account identity, balances, positions, or risk policy.
+
+## 14. Required Risk Facts
+
+The current Risk Domain consumes factual inputs including:
+
+- balance;
+- equity;
+- used and free margin;
+- daily-start balance;
+- daily closed PnL;
+- open positions;
+- position market value;
+- position loss at stop;
+- position margin;
+- current market prices;
+- proposed notional and expected loss;
+- required margin.
+
+Evidence:
+
+- `risk-domain/src/main/java/com/hope/trading/risk/snapshot/AccountSnapshot.java:8-27`
+- `risk-domain/src/main/java/com/hope/trading/risk/snapshot/PositionSnapshot.java:8-22`
+- `risk-domain/src/main/java/com/hope/trading/risk/metric/ObservedMetricsCalculator.java:6-12`
+- `risk-domain/src/main/java/com/hope/trading/risk/metric/ProjectionEngine.java:14-38`
+- `trading-core/src/main/java/com/hope/trading/trading_core/risk/application/TradePlanRiskEvaluationService.java:154-200`
+
+The authority matrix is:
+
+| Fact | LIVE authority | PAPER authority | Market Data required? |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Balances | Broker Service/provider | Local AccountBalance | No |
+| Equity | Provider facts plus valuation | Local state plus valuation | Often |
+| Used margin | Provider facts | Explicit supported PAPER calculation | As defined by calculation |
+| Daily start balance | Provider ledger/baseline | Local baseline or local ledger | Possibly |
+| Daily closed PnL | Provider trades/ledger | Local closed Trade/execution state | For conversion only |
+| Open exposure | Provider positions | Local OPEN Trade state | No |
+| Entry basis | Provider position | Local Trade/fill state | No |
+| Position value | Provider state plus valuation | Local exposure plus valuation | Yes |
+| Position risk/protection | Provider protective facts | Explicit local PAPER representation | Possibly |
+| Current price | Provider/market snapshot | Market Data | Yes |
+| Required margin | Broker-neutral authoritative source | Explicit supported PAPER source | Usually |
+| Provider position reference | Provider | Not applicable | No |
+
+The ADR does not invent PAPER margin, fee, slippage, or protective-stop
+semantics. Those remain implementation dependencies or separate decisions.
+
+## 15. Required Margin Gap
+
+The current required-margin implementation is deliberately unavailable:
+
+- `UnavailableRequiredMarginClient.java:7-13`
+
+It returns an empty result until an authoritative broker-neutral margin read
+exists. This can independently prevent complete T0/T1 evaluation.
+
+The required behavior is:
+
+```text
+missing required margin
+    -> risk context unavailable
+    -> no authorization
+```
+
+It must not become zero by default. Margin architecture is an implementation
+dependency and is not expanded by this ADR.
+
+## 16. T0 Identity Flow
+
+T0 SHALL use the financial Account identity:
+
+```text
+RiskEvaluation.Command.accountId
+    -> Account.accountId
+    -> Account ownership validation
+    -> canonical BrokerAccount relation
+    -> provider/mode validation
+    -> mode-aware Risk Facts source
+    -> immutable RiskEvaluationContext
+    -> Risk Domain
+```
+
+The risk configuration and assigned profile are keyed by the same financial
+Account ID. The linked BrokerAccount ID is used for routing and external facts,
+not as a substitute Account ID.
+
+## 17. T1 Identity Flow
+
+T1 SHALL resolve the same financial Account as T0.
+
+The target flow is:
+
+```text
+ExecutionIntent
+    + brokerAccountId
+    |     = routing identity
+    |
+    + TradePlanReference
+          -> TradePlan.tradingAccountId
+                = financial Account identity
+          -> Account
+          -> canonical BrokerAccount relation
+          -> relation must match intent.brokerAccountId
+          -> mode-aware Risk Facts source
+          -> T1 RiskEvaluationContext
+```
+
+The current behavior is incorrect:
+
+```text
+intent.brokerAccountId
+    -> AccountRepository.findById
+```
+
+The T1 risk persistence record must store the financial Account ID in its
+`account_id` field. Unavailable/error persistence must not substitute the
+BrokerAccount ID where the financial Account ID is known.
+
+## 18. Settlement Identity Consequence
+
+PAPER settlement must eventually resolve the same canonical financial Account
+used by T0 and T1:
+
+```text
+ExecutionIntent.brokerAccountId
+    -> canonical Account relation
+    -> Account financial state
+```
+
+`(owner, provider)` lookup is not an authoritative settlement mapping.
+
+Settlement implementation remains governed by ADR-042 and is not changed by
+this documentation ADR.
+
+## 19. Fail-Closed Behavior
+
+Required facts and configuration are mandatory inputs. The following conditions
+must prevent authorization:
+
+- financial Account missing;
+- canonical relation missing;
+- linked ownership inconsistent;
+- provider or execution mode inconsistent;
+- RiskConfiguration missing;
+- assigned RiskProfile missing;
+- RiskProfile invalid or incomplete;
+- required Market Data unavailable or incomplete;
+- required margin unavailable;
+- local PAPER state inconsistent;
+- required valuation impossible.
+
+Failures must remain distinguishable where practical:
+
+| Condition | Classification |
+|---|---|
+| Missing Account | Account/domain lookup failure |
+| Missing relation or inconsistent owner | Mapping/domain invariant failure |
+| Missing configuration/profile | Configuration unavailable |
+| Invalid profile | Configuration invalid |
+| Missing market input | Valuation unavailable |
+| Missing margin | Risk dependency unavailable |
+| Inconsistent local state | Domain/context invalid |
+
+No missing fact may silently become zero, empty exposure, unlimited risk, or a
+successful validation unless that value is proven authoritative.
+
+## 20. Security and Ownership
+
+Authorization must follow the complete identity chain:
+
+```text
+authenticated user
+    -> BrokerAccount.ownerId
+    -> linked Account.user.userId
+    -> Account financial state
+    -> risk configuration/profile
+    -> local PAPER positions
+```
+
+The application must validate ownership before exposing or mutating either
+account's state. A database relation alone is insufficient if it permits
+cross-user links.
+
+Provider and execution mode must be validated from the linked BrokerAccount,
+not accepted from an untrusted client as authoritative facts.
+
+## 21. Migration and Legacy Data
+
+This ADR introduces no migration. Future implementation requires:
+
+```text
+SCHEMA_CHANGE_REQUIRED = YES
+BACKFILL_REQUIRED = YES
+BACKFILL_DETERMINISTIC_FOR_ALL_ROWS = NO
+AMBIGUOUS_LEGACY_ROWS_POSSIBLE = YES
+```
+
+Provable backfill evidence may include:
+
+- existing `account_risk_configuration.broker_account_id`;
+- valid Account and BrokerAccount existence;
+- matching ownership;
+- matching provider;
+- consistent execution mode.
+
+`(owner, provider)` is not sufficient as a universal backfill key. Existing
+BrokerAccount rows can have the same owner/provider, while the Account model's
+`UNIQUE(user_id, broker)` constraint represents a different and narrower rule.
+
+The Story 0038 equal-UUID fixture is not migration evidence.
+
+Future migration must:
+
+- backfill only provable mappings;
+- quarantine or reject ambiguous rows;
+- require explicit manual resolution where necessary;
+- never choose the first matching account;
+- never reinterpret existing UUID meaning;
+- preserve existing LIVE external authority.
+
+## 22. Database Constraint Direction
+
+Future schema work should distinguish:
+
+### Database-enforceable invariants
+
+- foreign key from the canonical relation to `broker_account`;
+- first-milestone uniqueness for the one-to-one relationship;
+- required relation after a complete migration/provisioning transition;
+- existence of the linked Account and BrokerAccount.
+
+### Domain/application invariants
+
+- Account owner equals BrokerAccount owner;
+- provider metadata consistency;
+- execution-mode lifecycle validity;
+- risk readiness;
+- mode-correct fact routing;
+- complete and trustworthy local PAPER facts.
+
+The existing `UNIQUE(user_id, broker)` constraint must be explicitly reviewed
+and safely replaced or relaxed during implementation if multiple accounts for a
+provider are supported. It is not changed by this ADR.
+
+## 23. Alternatives Considered: Identity
+
+### A. Same Account/BrokerAccount UUID
+
+Rejected.
+
+- the entities have different responsibilities;
+- production creates independent identifiers;
+- equality hides incorrect lookups;
+- it couples financial identity to execution routing;
+- Story 0038 demonstrates the resulting false confidence.
+
+### B. Explicit durable relation
+
+Accepted.
+
+- explicit and auditable;
+- deterministic;
+- supports multiple accounts;
+- preserves distinct identities;
+- allows ownership/provider/mode invariants to be validated.
+
+### C. `(owner, provider)` lookup
+
+Rejected as canonical identity.
+
+- ambiguous with multiple accounts;
+- does not identify a financial Account;
+- current Account and BrokerAccount uniqueness rules differ;
+- cannot safely support LIVE/PAPER coexistence.
+
+### D. Dedicated identity entity or value object
+
+Deferred.
+
+The first milestone does not justify another abstraction if an explicit one-to-
+one relation is sufficient. A future identity abstraction may be introduced if
+the relationship becomes more complex than the current model supports.
+
+## 24. Alternatives Considered: Risk Facts
+
+### A. Use `BrokerRiskFactsPort` for every mode
+
+Rejected as the long-term semantic boundary.
+
+It gives Broker Service/provider facts authority over PAPER state and requires
+credentials or an external account that PAPER does not possess.
+
+### B. Neutral mode-aware Risk Facts boundary
+
+Accepted.
+
+It preserves the distinction between factual inputs and risk interpretation and
+supports both external LIVE facts and local PAPER facts.
+
+### C. Router above the existing LIVE adapter
+
+Accepted as a staged implementation technique.
+
+The existing LIVE adapter can remain while a mode-aware router selects a local
+PAPER source.
+
+### D. Mode branching inside the Risk Domain
+
+Rejected.
+
+It would make the deterministic Risk Domain aware of infrastructure and
+execution providers. Mode belongs to fact acquisition, not rule interpretation.
+
+## 25. Alternatives Considered: PAPER Risk Configuration
+
+### A. Promote legacy Rules automatically
+
+Rejected.
+
+Legacy `Rules` are not versioned `RiskProfile` records and have no approved
+translation or provenance path.
+
+### B. Require explicit valid profile assignment
+
+Accepted for the first milestone.
+
+It is fail-closed and does not invent limits.
+
+### C. Copy a profile from another account
+
+Rejected/deferred.
+
+It creates hidden policy inheritance and ambiguous provenance.
+
+### D. Automatically create a versioned default profile
+
+Deferred until a default policy and its limits are explicitly authorized.
+
+## 26. Architectural Invariants
+
+```text
+ACCOUNT_FINANCIAL_IDENTITY_IS_DISTINCT_FROM_BROKER_ROUTING_IDENTITY
+
+ACCOUNT_TO_BROKERACCOUNT_RELATION_IS_EXPLICIT_AND_DURABLE
+
+FIRST_MILESTONE_ACCOUNT_TO_BROKERACCOUNT_CARDINALITY_IS_ONE_TO_ONE
+
+ACCOUNT_OWNERSHIP_EQUALS_LINKED_BROKERACCOUNT_OWNERSHIP
+
+CROSS_USER_ACCOUNT_RELATIONS_ARE_REJECTED
+
+ACCOUNT_PROVIDER_MATCHES_LINKED_BROKERACCOUNT_PROVIDER
+
+EXECUTION_MODE_IS_RESOLVED_FROM_THE_LINKED_BROKERACCOUNT
+
+ACCOUNT_LOOKUP_DOES_NOT_DEPEND_ON_OWNER_PROVIDER_AMBIGUITY
+
+ACCOUNT_ID_EQUALITY_IS_NOT_USED_AS_IMPLICIT_MAPPING
+
+MULTIPLE_ACCOUNTS_DO_NOT_CREATE_AMBIGUOUS_LOOKUPS
+
+RISK_CONFIGURATION_IS_EXPLICIT_VERSIONED_AND_RELOADABLE
+
+LEGACY_RULES_ARE_NOT_IMPLICITLY_EQUIVALENT_TO_RISK_PROFILES
+
+RISK_FACTS_SOURCE_IS_MODE_CORRECT
+
+LIVE_RISK_FACTS_PRESERVE_EXTERNAL_PROVIDER_AUTHORITY
+
+PAPER_RISK_FACTS_USE_LOCAL_TRADING_CORE_AUTHORITY
+
+PAPER_RISK_FACTS_DO_NOT_REQUIRE_BROKER_CREDENTIALS
+
+PAPER_MUST_NOT_CALL_BROKER_SERVICE_FOR_FINANCIAL_OR_POSITION_FACTS
+
+MARKET_DATA_PROVIDES_VALUATION_INPUTS_NOT_ACCOUNT_AUTHORITY
+
+RISK_DOMAIN_REMAINS_FACT_SOURCE_AGNOSTIC
+
+RISK_AUTHORITY_DOES_NOT_CHANGE_BY_EXECUTION_MODE
+
+MISSING_REQUIRED_RISK_FACTS_FAIL_CLOSED
+
+T0_AND_T1_RESOLVE_THE_SAME_FINANCIAL_ACCOUNT
+
+EXECUTION_INTENT_BROKER_ACCOUNT_ID_IS_NOT_A_FINANCIAL_ACCOUNT_ID
+
+ACCOUNT_RISK_CONFIGURATION_BROKER_ACCOUNT_ID_CANNOT_DRIFT_FROM_CANONICAL_RELATION
+```
+
+## 27. Relationship to Other ADRs
+
+### ADR-042
+
+ADR-042 remains authoritative for position authority and close semantics:
+
+```text
+LIVE_POSITION_AUTHORITY = BROKER
+PAPER_POSITION_AUTHORITY = TRADING_CORE
+```
+
+ADR-043 provides the account identity and facts-source architecture required to
+make that distinction executable safely. It does not supersede ADR-042 and does
+not decide PAPER position query, exit, or settlement implementation.
+
+### ADR-028
+
+```text
+ADR_028_COMPATIBLE = YES
+ADR_028_AMENDMENT_REQUIRED = NO
+```
+
+ADR-028 already requires immutable context, fact acquisition outside the Risk
+Domain, deterministic interpretation, provenance, and fail-closed behavior.
+ADR-043 changes where context facts are acquired, not who interprets them.
+
+An amendment is required only if later implementation changes risk-rule
+semantics, result meanings, fail-closed behavior, or introduces new rule
+categories.
+
+### ADR-029
+
+ADR-029 remains authoritative for execution lifecycle, idempotency, attempts,
+orders, reconciliation, and execution audit. `ExecutionIntent.brokerAccountId`
+continues to identify execution routing and must not be repurposed as a
+financial Account ID.
+
+### ADR-041
+
+```text
+ADR_041_COMPATIBLE = YES
+ADR_041_AMENDMENT_REQUIRED = NO
+```
+
+ADR-043 preserves:
+
+- human authorization;
+- mandatory server-side T1;
+- separate T0/T1 provenance;
+- LIVE external authority;
+- fail-closed safety.
+
+ADR-041 contains contradictory implementation-status statements about T1. That
+is documentation debt and is not rewritten by this ADR.
+
+## 28. Scope Boundary
+
+This ADR does not decide or implement:
+
+- PAPER position-query implementation;
+- PAPER EXIT implementation;
+- PAPER realized-PnL settlement;
+- universal Position aggregate;
+- simulation realism;
+- fees, slippage, latency, or partial fills;
+- pending orders;
+- cTrader integration;
+- FTMO rules;
+- frontend UX;
+- automatic profile inheritance;
+- final default risk limits;
+- new Risk Domain rules;
+- changes to `RiskValidationResult` semantics;
+- backtesting or historical replay.
+
+## 29. Future Implementation Tests
+
+No tests are created by this ADR. Future implementation must prove:
+
+### Identity
+
+- application-created Account and BrokerAccount have distinct IDs;
+- the explicit relation resolves the correct Account;
+- multiple accounts for one provider are unambiguous;
+- cross-user relations are rejected;
+- provider/mode mismatches are rejected;
+- missing relations fail closed.
+
+### Risk Configuration
+
+- explicit profile assignment survives reload;
+- legacy Rules alone are insufficient;
+- missing/invalid configuration blocks evaluation;
+- no implicit unlimited or zero policy is created.
+
+### PAPER Facts
+
+- PAPER T0 and T1 use local financial facts;
+- PAPER evaluation makes zero Broker Service financial/position-facts calls;
+- Market Data is used only for valuation inputs;
+- missing local facts fail closed.
+
+### LIVE Regression
+
+- LIVE T0 and T1 preserve Broker Service/provider authority;
+- local PAPER routing does not alter LIVE facts or reconciliation.
+
+### T0/T1 Identity
+
+- both evaluations use the same financial Account ID;
+- `ExecutionIntent.brokerAccountId` remains routing identity;
+- T1 persists financial Account ID;
+- distinct-ID execution succeeds without fixture aliasing.
+
+### Restart
+
+```text
+create PAPER account
+    -> persist
+    -> reload
+    -> relation/profile intact
+    -> deterministic risk evaluation remains possible
+```
+
+## 30. Story Boundary Consequence
+
+No Engineering Story is created by this ADR.
+
+The originally proposed Story “Establish PAPER Account Identity and Risk Facts”
+is too broad as one implementation slice and should be split after ADR review:
+
+### Future Story A - Account Identity and Provisioning
+
+Conceptual scope:
+
+- canonical Account-to-BrokerAccount relation;
+- first-milestone one-to-one constraints;
+- ownership/provider/mode invariants;
+- migration and backfill handling;
+- PAPER account provisioning;
+- explicit risk configuration/profile readiness.
+
+### Future Story B - Mode-Aware Risk Facts and T0/T1
+
+Conceptual scope:
+
+- neutral Risk Facts boundary;
+- LIVE adapter preservation;
+- local PAPER facts;
+- mode-aware routing;
+- T0 identity path;
+- T1 identity correction;
+- fail-closed missing facts;
+- distinct-ID integration proof.
+
+No Story numbers are assigned by this ADR.
+
+## 31. LEARN / PAIR / DELEGATE
+
+### LEARN
+
+- Account versus BrokerAccount identity: exercises aggregate boundaries and
+  domain identity design.
+- JPA cardinality and ownership: exercises owning sides, foreign keys, nullable
+  relations, and uniqueness.
+- Database constraints and backfill: exercises safe schema evolution and
+  ambiguity handling.
+- RiskConfiguration versus RiskFacts: exercises policy/state separation and
+  deterministic context assembly.
+- Risk snapshot completeness: exercises immutable input contracts and
+  fail-closed behavior.
+- Local PAPER financial facts: exercises deterministic balances, positions, and
+  valuation.
+- Transaction and failure semantics: exercises Spring transaction ownership and
+  financial consistency.
+
+### PAIR
+
+- canonical relation and cardinality;
+- mode-aware Risk Facts routing;
+- T0/T1 identity correction;
+- fail-closed error classification;
+- legacy migration policy.
+
+These choices affect financial safety and future provider compatibility.
+
+### DELEGATE
+
+After the architecture is accepted and learned concepts are validated:
+
+- mechanical migration SQL;
+- repetitive JPA and repository plumbing;
+- repetitive adapter wiring;
+- fixture updates;
+- later neutral API and Angular wiring.
+
+## 32. Final Decision Summary
+
+```text
+ACCOUNT_IDS_DISTINCT = YES
+
+CANONICAL_ACCOUNT_RELATION = EXPLICIT_DURABLE_ACCOUNT_TO_BROKERACCOUNT
+
+FIRST_MILESTONE_CARDINALITY = 1:1
+
+ACCOUNT_OWNERSHIP_INVARIANT =
+    ACCOUNT_USER_ID_EQUALS_LINKED_BROKERACCOUNT_OWNER_ID
+

+    LEGACY_ACCOUNT_PROVIDER_METADATA_MUST_AGREE_WITH_BROKERACCOUNT_PROVIDER
+

+

+

+    NEUTRAL_MODE_AWARE_BOUNDARY_OUTSIDE_RISK_DOMAIN
+

+

+### 8.2 Public API Direction
+
+The current endpoint was designed for LIVE broker identity:
+
+```text
+POST /api/v1/accounts/{accountId}/positions/close
+body: { brokerPositionReference }
+```
+
+Future implementation SHOULD evolve this toward a neutral product position
+target while preserving the stable product action. A mode-neutral response may
+share common status fields, but it must not falsely claim identical convergence
+semantics:
+
+- LIVE may remain pending until provider reconciliation confirms exposure state;
+- PAPER can reach local CLOSED after the local transaction commits;
+- LIVE and PAPER failure/recovery evidence comes from different authorities.
+
+The API change is not implemented by this ADR.
+
+## 9. PAPER Close Semantics
+
+### 9.1 Decision
+
+PAPER full close SHALL be represented as an explicit exit execution intent that
+uses the common execution concepts but a local PAPER authority.
+
+```text
+OPEN PAPER position
+    -> human ClosePosition request
+    -> resolve local target and current quantity
+    -> create EXIT execution intent
+    -> deterministic reducing-exit validation
+    -> simulated opposite-side execution
+    -> BrokerOrder + Fill
+    -> local PAPER settlement
+    -> close target Trade and realize PnL
+```
+
+The first implementation SHALL support:
+
+```text
+FULL_CLOSE_ONLY
+NO_PARTIAL_CLOSE
+NO_EXPOSURE_REVERSAL
+```
+
+### 9.2 Why Not `PositionCloseCommand` for PAPER
+
+`PositionCloseCommand` is retained for LIVE because it assumes:
+
+- broker position identity;
+- provider mutation-scope resolution;
+- Broker Service execution;
+- provider-authoritative reload;
+- external reconciliation.
+
+Those assumptions are not true for PAPER. PAPER must not be routed through
+`BrokerPositionCloseAdapter`, `BrokerPositionCloseClient`, or Broker Service
+mutation capabilities merely to reuse a command name or state machine.
+
+The lifecycle principles of human authorization, ownership, idempotency,
+unknown-outcome safety, and explicit audit may be reused conceptually. The
+authority and mutation mechanism may not.
+
+### 9.3 Local Target Resolution
+
+Before creating or applying a PAPER EXIT, Trading Core SHALL:
+
+- authenticate the caller;
+- verify ownership of the financial account and local position;
+- reload the current local position state;
+- verify that it is OPEN;
+- derive the current side and quantity server-side;
+- claim or reserve the target against a competing close;
+- reject if the target no longer exists or is already closed.
+
+The frontend must not be authoritative for side, quantity, entry price, or
+financial state.
+
+## 10. Entry and Exit Intent Semantics
+
+### 10.1 Explicit Purpose
+
+Side alone is not sufficient to express the meaning of an execution:
+
+```text
+SELL may open/increase short exposure or close long exposure
+BUY  may open/increase long exposure or close short exposure
+```
+
+The execution model SHALL distinguish at least:
+
+```text
+ExecutionPurpose = ENTRY | EXIT
+```
+
+The exact Java type and persistence shape are left to implementation, but the
+semantic distinction is mandatory for a PAPER exit.
+
+### 10.2 EXIT Target
+
+An EXIT intent SHALL identify the local target exposure/Trade and the requested
+close quantity. For the first milestone:
+
+- target quantity is the complete current quantity;
+- target side is reloaded server-side;
+- execution side is derived as its opposite;
+- quantity greater than current exposure is rejected;
+- an EXIT cannot create a new opposite OPEN Trade.
+
+### 10.3 Lifecycle Reuse Boundary
+
+The current `ExecutionIntent` is entry-oriented and requires TradePlan and risk
+approval references. It SHALL NOT be reused unchanged if that forces entry-only
+prerequisites onto a PAPER close.
+
+Implementation may either:
+
+- generalize `ExecutionIntent` with explicit purpose and optional exit target;
+- introduce an exit-specific execution authorization that reuses the common
+  attempt/order/fill/audit mechanisms; or
+- use another equivalent design that preserves the invariants of this ADR.
+
+This ADR chooses the semantic requirement, not an implementation class shape.
+
+## 11. Exit Risk Semantics
+
+### 11.1 Common Authority
+
+Risk remains deterministic, explainable, auditable, and fail-closed under ADR-
+028. AI cannot approve, override, or alter a PAPER exit.
+
+### 11.2 Reducing Exit Is Not Entry
+
+An exit is a position-reducing action, not a new TradePlan entry. The first
+PAPER close SHALL NOT require the existing entry TradePlan/T0 approval as a
+prerequisite, consistent with ADR-040's distinction for position reduction.
+
+It SHALL still undergo deterministic safety validation for:
+
+- authenticated ownership;
+- PAPER mode and local authority;
+- target existence and OPEN state;
+- current side and quantity;
+- no over-close or reversal;
+- current market-data availability for simulation;
+- account consistency;
+- active close/idempotency conflicts;
+- explicit human authorization.
+
+### 11.3 T1-Like Validation
+
+A fresh deterministic reducing-exit validation SHOULD occur immediately before
+the simulated financial mutation. It may use an exit-specific validation mode
+or an equivalent context, but it must not apply entry-only exposure-increase
+rules in a way that prevents a safe full reduction.
+
+If the exit model introduces new Risk Domain rule categories or changes the
+meaning of RiskValidationResult, ADR-028/ADR-041 must be amended before
+implementation.
+
+### 11.4 Risk Facts Dependency
+
+This ADR does not decide the Account/BrokerAccount identity or PAPER risk-facts
+source. A separate decision must define how the Risk Domain receives complete
+local PAPER facts. This ADR requires only that the eventual source be trusted,
+deterministic, mode-correct, and compatible with fail-closed risk authority.
+
+## 12. Settlement Semantics
+
+### 12.1 Entry
+
+For a successful PAPER ENTRY:
+
+```text
+entry Fill
+    -> mutate authoritative local balances
+    -> open/increase matching local exposure
+    -> persist order, fill, Account, and Trade state
+```
+
+The current baseline semantics remain:
+
+- BUY debits quote value plus fee and credits base quantity;
+- SELL debits base quantity and credits quote value minus fee;
+- current simulator fees are zero;
+- BUY uses ask and SELL uses bid.
+
+### 12.2 Holding
+
+The authoritative persisted state is quantity, side, entry basis, balances,
+and lifecycle. Current price and unrealized PnL SHOULD be dynamically projected
+from a timestamped Market Data snapshot rather than persisted on every tick.
+
+For one exposure:
+
+```text
+long unrealizedPnL  = (currentPrice - entryPrice) * quantity
+short unrealizedPnL = (entryPrice - currentPrice) * quantity
+```
+
+Marked equity is a deterministic valuation of local balances and exposure. It
+must not be confused with the current baseline implementation, which only
+subtracts fees in `PaperSettlementService.recalculateEquity()`.
+
+### 12.3 Exit
+
+For a successful full PAPER EXIT:
+
+```text
+exit Fill
+    -> reload target OPEN exposure
+    -> assert opposite side and full quantity
+    -> mutate balances
+    -> calculate realized PnL
+    -> set exitPrice and closedAt
+    -> set target Trade CLOSED
+    -> update realized Account state
+    -> persist exit order/fill and final local state
+```
+
+For a long:
+
+```text
+realizedPnL = (exitPrice - entryPrice) * quantity - fees
+```
+
+For a short:
+
+```text
+realizedPnL = (entryPrice - exitPrice) * quantity - fees
+```
+
+The first milestone does not define a new fee policy, multi-lot allocation
+policy, or provider-specific accounting behavior.
+
+## 13. Transaction and Atomicity Boundary
+
+### 13.1 Current Concern
+
+The current PAPER acknowledged-result path is not demonstrated as one atomic
+local transaction:
+
+```text
+ExecuteTradeService                         no transaction annotation
+    -> PaperSettlementService                transactional
+    -> BrokerOrder persistence                transactional adapter
+    -> ExecutionAttempt and Intent persistence
+```
+
+Evidence:
+
+- `trading-core/src/main/java/com/hope/trading/trading_core/execution/application/service/ExecuteTradeService.java`
+- `trading-core/src/main/java/com/hope/trading/trading_core/execution/application/service/PaperSettlementService.java:31-57`
+- `trading-core/src/main/java/com/hope/trading/trading_core/execution/application/pipeline/ExecutionFinalizationStep.java:45-69`
+- Story 0038's explicit limitation in `implementation-report.md:29-40`
+
+`PaperSettlementService` also silently returns if the broker account or
+financial account is missing, while finalization can continue.
+
+### 13.2 Decision
+
+For PAPER local financial application, the following effects SHALL have one
+transaction owner and commit atomically:
+
+```text
+BrokerOrder
+Fill
+Account balance mutation
+Trade/position mutation
+ExecutionAttempt finalization
+ExecutionIntent finalization
+settlement-effect idempotency state, if required
+```
+
+The current market-data lookup remains outside the database transaction. LIVE
+remote broker calls remain outside long database transactions as required by
+ADR-041.
+
+### 13.3 Failure
+
+If simulation acknowledges but local settlement fails, the system SHALL NOT
+report successful completion while financial state is absent. It must either:
+
+- roll back the local acknowledged-result transaction completely; or
+- persist an explicit recoverable state that blocks unsafe retry and identifies
+  the recovery action.
+
+For the first deterministic local PAPER implementation, complete local rollback
+is preferred where technically possible.
+
+## 14. Idempotency
+
+### 14.1 Shared Principles
+
+The existing Execution Domain principles remain applicable:
+
+- one human action maps to one logical execution;
+- idempotency identity is immutable;
+- terminal execution cannot be submitted again;
+- only one active attempt exists;
+- uncertain financial outcomes are not blindly retried.
+
+Evidence: `ADR-029`, `ADR-041`,
+`trading-core/src/main/java/com/hope/trading/trading_core/execution/domain/`.
+
+### 14.2 PAPER Entry
+
+PAPER ENTRY reuses the existing `ExecutionIntent` idempotency model. Settlement
+must not apply the same intent twice even if finalization is retried.
+
+### 14.3 PAPER Exit
+
+PAPER EXIT SHALL satisfy:
+
+```text
+same ClosePosition idempotency key
+    -> one exit authorization
+    -> one target claim
+    -> one financial settlement
+```
+
+An already CLOSED target cannot be closed again. A competing exit for the same
+target must be rejected deterministically. A separate persistence guard should
+be added only if the generalized execution identity cannot itself prove that
+the financial effect was applied.
+
+### 14.4 Unknown and Retry
+
+PAPER immediate simulation has no external provider unknown state. Local
+transaction failure is not equivalent to a broker timeout. It must follow local
+rollback/recovery semantics and must not be mislabeled as LIVE provider
+reconciliation.
+
+## 15. Position Query Boundary
+
+The position query service SHALL select its source by execution mode:
+
+```text
+PositionQueryService
+        |
+        +--> LIVE  -> Broker Service/provider projection
+        |
+        +--> PAPER -> local Account/Trade projection + Market Data valuation
+```
+
+The public position DTO SHOULD remain mode-neutral. It may expose an execution
+mode or source marker if required for user explanation, but must not require:
+
+- Kraken txids for PAPER;
+- cTrader position IDs for PAPER;
+- provider mutation scopes;
+- Broker Service credentials.
+
+The frontend SHALL request the product action “close this position.” It must
+not construct provider-specific mutation mechanics.
+
+## 16. LIVE Compatibility
+
+This decision preserves LIVE behavior:
+
+- Trading Core does not become authoritative for LIVE positions.
+- LIVE close remains under ADR-040's position-management capability.
+- Broker Service remains responsible for provider translation and reconciliation.
+- Kraken FIFO and `reduce_only` remain Broker Service/provider concerns.
+- Future cTrader position IDs and hedged/netted semantics remain provider
+  concerns.
+- LIVE provider references do not leak into PAPER domain semantics.
+- PAPER never calls Broker Service mutation or `BrokerPositionCloseClient`.
+- No FTMO or prop-firm concept is introduced into the core domain.
+
+## 17. Architectural Invariants
+
+The following invariants are adopted for mode-specific position management:
+
+```text
+LIVE_POSITION_AUTHORITY = BROKER
+PAPER_POSITION_AUTHORITY = TRADING_CORE
+
+PAPER_NEVER_CALLS_LIVE_MUTATION_BOUNDARY
+PAPER_EXIT_IS_HUMAN_AUTHORIZED
+PAPER_EXIT_HAS_EXPLICIT_PURPOSE_AND_LOCAL_TARGET
+PAPER_EXIT_CANNOT_INCREASE_EXPOSURE
+PAPER_FULL_EXIT_ONLY_FOR_INITIAL_ROUND_TRIP
+PAPER_FULL_EXIT_IS_IDEMPOTENT
+PAPER_FINANCIAL_STATE_IS_RELOADABLE
+PAPER_ENTRY_AND_EXIT_USE_DETERMINISTIC_EXECUTION
+PAPER_SETTLEMENT_CANNOT_SILENTLY_COMPLETE_WITHOUT_FINANCIAL_STATE
+PAPER_LOCAL_OPEN_AND_CLOSED_STATE_IS_AUTHORITATIVE
+RISK_REMAINS_DETERMINISTIC_AND_FAIL_CLOSED
+REDUCING_EXIT_DOES_NOT_REQUIRE_ENTRY_ONLY_RISK_PREREQUISITES
+MODE_SPECIFIC_FACTS_DO_NOT_CHANGE_RISK_AUTHORITY
+BROKER_PROVIDER_SEMANTICS_DO_NOT_LEAK_INTO_PAPER
+LIVE_RECONCILIATION_REMAINS_PROVIDER_AWARE
+PAPER_IS_NOT_BACKTESTING
+```
+
+## 18. Scope Boundary
+
+This ADR does NOT decide or implement:
+
+- Account/BrokerAccount identity or migration;
+- PAPER Risk Facts source/configuration;
+- changes to risk rule definitions;
+- a universal Position aggregate;
+- partial close;
+- SL/TP modification or automatic triggering;
+- trailing stops;
+- fees, slippage, latency, liquidity, or partial fills;
+- pending-order simulation;
+- cTrader implementation;
+- FTMO or prop-firm integration;
+- backtesting or historical replay;
+- TradeOutcome strategy analytics;
+- event sourcing;
+- WebSocket/SSE position streaming;
+- redesign of LIVE close behavior.
+
+## 19. Consequences
+
+### Positive
+
+- Position authority is explicit for both execution modes.
+- PAPER can remain independent of external credentials and provider state.
+- LIVE broker authority and reconciliation remain intact.
+- PAPER exit can reuse common execution, order, fill, audit, and idempotency
+  concepts without reusing provider-specific close commands.
+- A single product-level close action remains possible without misleading the
+  frontend about provider mechanics.
+- Full-close/no-reversal semantics protect the first PAPER round trip.
+- The first PAPER model remains small by retaining `Trade` rather than adding a
+  universal Position aggregate.
+- Future cTrader compatibility is preserved by keeping provider mechanics below
+  Broker Service.
+
+### Accepted Costs
+
+- A mode-aware product close boundary is required.
+- Execution authorization must distinguish ENTRY and EXIT.
+- Local PAPER position targeting and settlement require additional persistence
+  invariants.
+- PAPER and LIVE have different completion and reconciliation semantics.
+- A separate Account identity/risk-facts decision is required before safe
+  implementation.
+- Existing transaction and close-path debt remains visible rather than hidden.
+
+## 20. Alternatives Considered
+
+### A. Reuse `PositionCloseCommand` for PAPER
+
+Rejected. It would import broker identity, mutation scope, external
+reconciliation, and Broker Service authority into a Trading Core-owned local
+simulation.
+
+### B. Use a bare opposite-side execution with no explicit purpose
+
+Rejected. BUY/SELL side does not distinguish opening exposure from closing it.
+Without an explicit purpose and target, settlement can create an opposite OPEN
+Trade instead of closing the selected position.
+
+### C. Create a dedicated PAPER close command that duplicates execution
+
+Rejected for the first milestone. It would duplicate idempotency, attempts,
+orders, fills, audit, and human authorization unless it eventually delegates
+back to the common execution model.
+
+### D. Use a shared `ClosePosition` boundary with mode-specific implementations
+
+Accepted. It preserves a coherent product concept while keeping authority and
+mutation mechanics separate.
+
+### E. Introduce a universal persistent Position aggregate
+
+Rejected for now. LIVE remains broker-authoritative and the repository does not
+show a current requirement for a universal local position identity.
+
+### F. Use owner/provider lookup as the PAPER position target
+
+Rejected. It is ambiguous for multiple accounts and cannot identify one local
+exposure safely.
+
+### G. Require full entry T0 risk evaluation for every exit
+
+Rejected. A reducing exit is not an entry and entry-only exposure-increase
+rules must not make safe reduction impossible. Deterministic reducing-exit
+validation remains mandatory.
+
+### H. Add simulation realism before position lifecycle
+
+Rejected. Fees, slippage, partial fills, and latency do not make an entry-only
+PAPER path a usable validation environment.
+
+## 21. Implementation Impact
+
+This ADR is documentation only. Future implementation impact is classified
+below; no item is implemented by this decision.
+
+| Area | Classification | Direction |
+|---|---|---|
+| Position authority | DOMAIN | Keep LIVE broker authority and PAPER Core authority explicit |
+| Entry/exit purpose | DOMAIN / APPLICATION | Distinguish ENTRY and EXIT semantics |
+| Close product boundary | APPLICATION / API | Route one neutral ClosePosition action by mode |
+| PAPER exit | APPLICATION / PORT | Use exit execution intent and local target |
+| LIVE close | APPLICATION / ADAPTER | Preserve PositionCloseCommand and Broker Service path |
+| Local position | DOMAIN / PERSISTENCE | Retain `Trade` as minimal PAPER projection |
+| Settlement | APPLICATION / DOMAIN | Match exit target and realize local PnL |
+| Position query | APPLICATION / API | Select broker or local source by mode |
+| Risk exit validation | RISK / APPLICATION | Add reducing-exit context without bypassing authority |
+| Atomicity | APPLICATION / PERSISTENCE | One transaction owner for local financial effects |
+| Idempotency | DOMAIN / PERSISTENCE | Protect target claim and one settlement effect |
+| Account identity | DOMAIN / PERSISTENCE | Separate ADR; not decided here |
+| PAPER risk facts | PORT / ADAPTER | Separate ADR; not decided here |
+| Frontend | FRONTEND | Keep a neutral close action and mode-appropriate status |
+| Migration | MIGRATION | Future additive migrations only; no migration from this ADR |
+
+## 22. Testing Requirements for Future Implementation
+
+The implementation must prove, not merely assume:
+
+### PAPER entry
+
+```text
+application-created PAPER account
+    -> real local identity/risk setup
+    -> real deterministic T0/T1
+    -> simulated entry
+    -> persisted open Trade
+    -> reload
+```
+
+### PAPER position query
+
+```text
+PAPER -> local Trading Core source
+LIVE  -> Broker Service source
+```
+
+PAPER queries must produce zero Broker Service mutation calls.
+
+### PAPER exit
+
+```text
+open local PAPER Trade
+    -> human ClosePosition
+    -> EXIT target/purpose
+    -> reducing validation
+    -> simulated opposite fill
+    -> realized PnL
+    -> CLOSED Trade
+    -> persisted Account/order/fill state
+```
+
+Test both long-to-short-side-exit and short-to-long-side-exit, without allowing
+the exit to create opposite exposure.
+
+### Idempotency
+
+- same entry request produces one financial mutation;
+- same exit request produces one exit intent and one settlement;
+- already closed target rejects a second close;
+- competing active exit is rejected;
+- terminal intent cannot settle twice;
+- transaction failure does not duplicate balances or Trade transitions.
+
+### Failure atomicity
+
+Inject failures after fill construction and during local settlement/final
+persistence. Assert complete rollback or an explicit recoverable state; never a
+successful terminal state with missing financial mutation.
+
+### Restart
+
+```text
+entry -> reload -> query local position -> close
+      -> reload -> assert CLOSED + realized Account state
+```
+
+### LIVE regression
+
+Run Story 0033's existing LIVE position-close tests and verify that the new
+PAPER branch does not call Broker Service or change provider reconciliation.
+
+## 23. ADR Boundaries and Follow-up Decisions
+
+### Separate ADR required: Account Identity and PAPER Risk Facts
+
+A separate ADR is required before implementing the first PAPER risk/identity
+story. It must decide:
+
+- whether Account and BrokerAccount retain distinct IDs;
+- the canonical explicit relation between them;
+- multiple-account and uniqueness semantics;
+- how PAPER risk configuration is initialized and assigned;
+- the mode-aware source of T0/T1 facts;
+- whether `BrokerRiskFactsPort` remains the public port name or is generalized;
+- migration/backfill behavior for existing LIVE accounts.
+
+This is broader than position close and is intentionally not hidden in ADR-042.
+
+### Possible ADR-028/041 Amendment
+
+Amend ADR-028 or ADR-041 only if reducing-exit validation changes the Risk
+Domain contract, introduces new rule categories, or changes fail-closed
+semantics. A new evaluation context using existing risk authority can remain a
+dependency of this ADR without a separate risk ADR.
+
+### No ADR required for mechanical work
+
+No new ADR is required merely for:
+
+- retaining `Trade` as the first local PAPER projection;
+- using current Market Data for deterministic valuation;
+- writing persistence tests;
+- keeping provider mechanics in Broker Service;
+- adding neutral API fields after this boundary is accepted.
+
+## 24. Migration and Rollout Constraints
+
+- This ADR introduces no schema migration.
+- Future migrations must be additive and explicitly backfillable.
+- No existing LIVE position data may be reinterpreted as local PAPER state.
+- No existing provider position reference may be stored as a PAPER mutation
+  target.
+- Existing Story 0038 fill migration `V11__persist_execution_broker_fills.sql`
+  remains valid and is not renamed by this ADR.
+- A future implementation must not silently change Account uniqueness semantics
+  while solving identity.
+
+## 25. Deferred Work
+
+The following remain explicitly deferred:
+
+- partial close;
+- SL/TP modification and automatic exits;
+- trailing stops;
+- fees, slippage, latency, partial fills, liquidity, and pending orders;
+- backtesting and historical replay;
+- strategy validation and parameter sweeps;
+- TradeOutcome strategy analytics;
+- automatic background reconciliation for PAPER;
+- universal Position aggregate;
+- cTrader and FTMO integration;
+- provider-specific semantics in Trading Core;
+- event sourcing and tick-level financial persistence.
+
+## 26. Open Questions
+
+These questions belong to the separate Account Identity/Risk Facts decision or
+future refinement:
+
+- Should the first local PAPER model support one net exposure per symbol only?
+- Should a neutral ClosePosition response expose a distinct local completion
+  status or normalize it with LIVE statuses?
+- Should exit authorization be an extended `ExecutionIntent` or a dedicated
+  exit command sharing execution effects?
+- Should local PAPER current valuations be persisted as snapshots for audit, or
+  remain dynamic projections with a timestamped source?
+- Is a separate accepted PAPER ADR useful after the identity/risk ADR, or are
+  these mode decisions sufficient?
+
+## 27. Consequences for Story Refinement
+
+No Engineering Story is created by this ADR. Once ADR-042 and the separate
+Account Identity/Risk Facts ADR are accepted and their open questions are
+resolved, the first implementation Story should remain:
+
+> Establish PAPER Account Identity and Risk Facts.
+
+The subsequent sequence should be:
+
+```text
+Account Identity and PAPER Risk Facts
+    -> local PAPER Position Query and Valuation
+    -> PAPER Full Exit through EXIT ExecutionIntent
+    -> persisted PAPER Round-Trip Regression
+```
+
+The sequence must not begin with simulation realism or cTrader integration.
+

+# ADR-043 - Account Identity and Mode-Specific Risk Facts
+
+## Status
+
+Accepted
+
+## Date
+
+2026-09-14
+
+## Decision Makers
+
+- Trading OS Architecture
+- Project Owner
+
+## Related ADRs
+
+- ADR-028 - Risk Engine Architecture
+- ADR-029 - Execution Domain Architecture
+- ADR-041 - Human-Controlled Trade Execution and Financial Command Safety
+- ADR-042 - Position Authority and Close Semantics by Execution Mode
+
+## Related Stories
+
+- Story 0037 - PAPER Account Web Wiring
+- Story 0038 - Persisted PAPER Execution Regression
+
+---
+
+## 1. Context
+
+Trading OS has two account concepts with different responsibilities:
+
+```text
+Account.accountId
+    = Trading Core financial account identity
+
+BrokerAccount.id
+    = execution and broker-routing identity
+```
+
+These identifiers are independently generated and represent different domain
+concepts. `Account` owns balances, equity, trades, and local financial state.
+`BrokerAccount` owns provider, execution mode, connection metadata, and routing
+identity.
+
+ADR-042 establishes the corresponding position authority boundary:
+
+```text
+LIVE  position authority = external broker/provider
+PAPER position authority = Trading Core
+```
+
+The repository currently has no direct durable relation between `Account` and
+`BrokerAccount`. It instead uses several incomplete or inconsistent mechanisms:
+
+- `AccountRiskConfiguration` contains both IDs but is not created by PAPER
+  account provisioning;
+- PAPER settlement searches by `(owner, provider)`;
+- T1 currently treats `ExecutionIntent.brokerAccountId` as an Account ID;
+- Story 0038 assigns the same UUID to both entities in its persistence fixture;
+- PAPER risk evaluation still uses the external `BrokerRiskFactsPort`.
+
+The result is that a PAPER account can be created and a simulated entry can be
+persisted, while the real T0/T1 risk path cannot reliably resolve the same
+logical financial account without test-only assumptions.
+
+## 2. Problem Statement
+
+The architecture must define:
+
+- distinct financial and execution identities;
+- the canonical durable relationship between them;
+- first-milestone cardinality and ownership invariants;
+- explicit PAPER risk configuration lifecycle;
+- mode-correct Risk Facts acquisition;
+- correct identity flow through T0 and T1;
+- fail-closed behavior when required facts or configuration are unavailable.
+
+The decision must not collapse `Account` and `BrokerAccount`, make provider
+lookup an identity mechanism, or move risk interpretation into infrastructure
+adapters.
+
+## 3. Repository Evidence
+
+### 3.1 Domain Entities
+
+`User` owns financial accounts through `Account.user`:
+
+- `trading-core/src/main/java/com/hope/trading/trading_core/model/User.java:21-45`
+
+`Account` has an independently generated UUID and owns balances, equity, rules,
+user, and trades:
+
+- `trading-core/src/main/java/com/hope/trading/trading_core/model/Account.java:21-74`
+
+`BrokerAccount` has an independently supplied/generated UUID, `ownerId`,
+provider, and execution mode:
+
+- `trading-core/src/main/java/com/hope/trading/trading_core/brokeraccount/domain/BrokerAccount.java:19-51`
+- `BrokerAccount.java:69-72`
+
+There is no JPA relation between the two entities.
+
+### 3.2 Database Model
+
+The baseline defines independent tables:
+
+- `accounts.account_id`: `V1__trading_core_clean_install_baseline.sql:22-31`
+- `broker_account.id`: `V1__trading_core_clean_install_baseline.sql:60-73`
+
+The risk configuration table contains:
+
+```text
+account_id          PRIMARY KEY, FK accounts(account_id)
+broker_account_id   NOT NULL, UNIQUE, no FK broker_account(id)
+```
+
+Evidence:
+
+- `V2__trade_plan_risk_evaluation.sql:27-33`
+- `RiskPersistence.java:286-293`
+
+The current account uniqueness constraint is:
+
+```text
+UNIQUE (user_id, broker)
+```
+
+Evidence:
+
+- `V7__accounts_unique_broker_per_user.sql:1-5`
+
+This constraint does not represent BrokerAccount identity or execution mode.
+
+### 3.3 PAPER Provisioning
+
+`BrokerAccountService.create()` creates a BrokerAccount and, for PAPER, a
+separate financial Account with initial USD balance and legacy `Rules`:
+
+- `BrokerAccountService.java:38-85`
+
+The financial Account receives a generated ID and no BrokerAccount reference.
+PAPER provisioning does not create:
+
+- `account_risk_configuration`;
+- `account_risk_profile_assignment`;
+- a versioned `risk_profile`;
+- a canonical Account-to-BrokerAccount relation.
+
+The legacy default values are created at:
+
+- `BrokerAccountService.java:87-100`
+
+Those values belong to the legacy `Rules` entity and are not automatically an
+assigned immutable `RiskProfile`.
+
+### 3.4 LIVE Synchronization
+
+The legacy LIVE synchronization path resolves a financial Account through:
+
+```text
+user + provider string
+```
+
+Evidence:
+
+- `BrokerSynchronizationServiceImpl.java:33-71`
+- `AccountRepository.java:10-14`
+
+The broker account identity is not used as the canonical financial Account
+mapping in this path.
+
+### 3.5 T0 Risk Evaluation
+
+T0 starts from the financial Account ID:
+
+```text
+RiskEvaluation.Command.accountId
+    -> AccountRepository.findById
+    -> Account ownership check
+    -> AccountRiskConfiguration(accountId)
+    -> linked BrokerAccount ownership check
+    -> assigned RiskProfile(accountId)
+    -> broker facts using configuration.brokerAccountId
+```
+
+Evidence:
+
+- `TradePlanRiskEvaluationService.java:131-151`
+- `TradePlanRiskEvaluationService.java:225-254`
+
+This is conceptually correct when the caller supplies the actual financial
+Account ID and the risk configuration exists.
+
+### 3.6 T1 Risk Revalidation
+
+T1 currently starts with:
+
+```java

+```
+
+and then loads `Account`, risk configuration, and profile using that value:
+
+- `ExecutionTimeRiskRevalidationService.java:127-141`
+
+It also compares:
+
+```java
+intent.brokerAccountId().equals(plan.tradingAccountId())
+```
+
+at:
+
+- `ExecutionTimeRiskRevalidationService.java:296-303`
+
+This compares execution/routing identity with financial account identity.
+
+### 3.7 Execution Intent
+
+`ExecutionIntent` explicitly stores `brokerAccountId`:
+
+- `execution/domain/aggregate/ExecutionIntent.java:10-20`
+- `ExecutionIntent.java:47-69`
+
+This field is passed to broker execution adapters and is therefore a routing
+identity, not a financial Account identity.
+
+`ValidateAndCreateService` already resolves the BrokerAccount from risk
+configuration keyed by the financial Account:
+
+- `ValidateAndCreateService.java:108-157`
+
+Its tests deliberately use distinct IDs:
+
+- `ValidateAndCreateServiceTest.java:41-46`
+- `ValidateAndCreateServiceTest.java:124-151`
+
+### 3.8 PAPER Settlement
+
+PAPER settlement resolves the BrokerAccount by intent ID and then resolves the
+financial Account by owner and provider:
+
+- `PaperSettlementService.java:31-48`
+
+This is not a canonical identity mapping.
+
+### 3.9 Story 0038 Fixture
+
+Story 0038 assigns:
+
+```java
+accountId = brokerAccountId;
+```
+
+in its persisted integration fixture:
+
+- `PaperExecutionPersistenceIntegrationTest.java:101-110`
+
+The same test replaces the real T1 service with a mock:
+
+- `PaperExecutionPersistenceIntegrationTest.java:76-91`
+
+The implementation report explicitly limits the test to persistence and
+external-boundary wiring:
+
+- `docs/architecture/stories/0038-persisted-paper-execution-regression/implementation-report.md:29-51`
+
+The equal UUID is test scaffolding and is not an architectural relationship.
+
+## 4. Decision
+
+Trading OS adopts the following identity model:
+
+```text
+Account.accountId
+    = financial Account identity
+
+BrokerAccount.id
+    = execution/routing identity
+
+Account -> BrokerAccount
+    = explicit durable canonical relation
+```
+
+The two identifiers SHALL remain distinct. Equal UUID values, if they occur by
+accident, SHALL NOT imply identity equivalence.
+
+No service SHALL use any of the following as the canonical relationship:
+
+- equality of the two UUIDs;
+- `(owner, provider)` lookup;
+- display name;
+- provider-specific external identifiers;
+- existence of a risk configuration row.
+
+The exact Java field or persistence representation is an implementation
+decision. The relation semantics are architectural and fixed by this ADR.
+
+## 5. Canonical Relationship Authority
+
+The canonical Account-to-BrokerAccount relation belongs to the account/domain
+model, independently of risk configuration.
+
+The current `account_risk_configuration.broker_account_id` SHALL NOT be the
+sole identity authority because:
+
+- risk configuration may not exist;
+- account identity exists independently of policy;
+- the column currently lacks a foreign key to `broker_account`;
+- PAPER account creation does not create the configuration;
+- risk policy lifecycle must not determine account identity lifecycle.
+
+If the current configuration column remains during migration, it SHALL be one
+of:
+
+- transitional mapping data; or
+- validated configuration metadata that cannot disagree with the canonical
+  Account relation.
+
+It SHALL NOT become a second independently mutable relationship.
+
+Required invariant:
+
+```text
+ACCOUNT_RISK_CONFIGURATION_BROKER_ACCOUNT_ID
+    CANNOT_DRIFT_FROM_CANONICAL_RELATION
+```
+
+## 6. Cardinality
+
+For the first milestone:
+
+```text
+Account 1 <-> 1 BrokerAccount
+```
+
+More precisely:
+
+- one financial Account maps to exactly one BrokerAccount;
+- one BrokerAccount maps to at most one canonical financial Account.
+
+This supports multiple accounts for one user and provider:
+
+```text
+User
+    +-- BrokerAccount A -> Account A
+    +-- BrokerAccount B -> Account B
+    +-- PAPER BrokerAccount -> PAPER Account
+```
+
+The architecture SHALL NOT introduce `BrokerAccount -> N financial Accounts`
+without a demonstrated product requirement for multiple financial views,
+portfolios, or policies over one external account.
+
+This first-milestone constraint remains evolvable through a future ADR.
+
+## 7. Ownership, Provider, and Mode Invariants
+
+### 7.1 Ownership
+
+The linked records must belong to the same authenticated owner:
+
+```text
+Account.user.userId == BrokerAccount.ownerId
+```
+
+Database foreign keys may enforce record existence, but cross-record owner
+consistency requires deterministic domain/application validation unless the
+schema is deliberately designed for composite enforcement.
+
+### 7.2 Provider
+
+`BrokerAccount.provider` is the provider authority.
+
+The legacy `Account.broker` string is metadata and must not become the new
+canonical provider identity. If retained during migration, it must agree with
+the linked BrokerAccount or be treated as stale/legacy data and rejected where
+provider correctness matters.
+
+### 7.3 Execution Mode
+
+Execution mode is authoritative on `BrokerAccount`:
+
+```text
+Account -> BrokerAccount -> executionMode
+```
+
+PAPER is an execution mode, not a `BrokerProvider`.
+
+No duplicate independently mutable execution mode is introduced on `Account`.
+
+## 8. Account Creation Invariant
+
+A newly usable trading account must establish the following logical graph:
+
+```text
+BrokerAccount
+    + financial Account
+    + canonical relation
+    + explicit RiskConfiguration
+    + assigned immutable RiskProfile
+        = risk-ready trading account
+```
+
+For PAPER, the following is insufficient:
+
+```text
+BrokerAccount exists
+    + legacy Rules exists
+```
+
+Account creation must not report a PAPER account as risk-ready unless the
+explicit configuration and profile requirements are satisfied or the account
+is clearly marked unavailable for trading.
+
+The exact local transaction/orchestration boundary remains implementation work.
+
+## 9. Risk Configuration
+
+`RiskConfiguration` represents policy and limits. It is separate from current
+financial state:
+
+```text
+RiskConfiguration
+    = policy, limits, version, assignment and provenance
+
+RiskFacts
+    = current factual account, position and market state
+
+RiskEngine
+    = deterministic interpretation and decision
+```
+
+PAPER SHALL require an explicit, versioned, persisted RiskProfile assignment
+before it is eligible for deterministic trading evaluation.
+
+The legacy `Rules` entity is not implicitly equivalent to the current
+
+- `Rules.java:16-49` is unversioned legacy configuration;
+- `RiskPersistence.java:259-301` models versioned immutable profiles and
+  assignments;
+- `V2__trade_plan_risk_evaluation.sql:1-43` defines the current schema.
+
+The current legacy values are not an authorized default policy for the current
+RiskProfile architecture.
+
+```text
+DEFAULTS_AUTHORIZED_BY_EXISTING_POLICY = NO
+```
+
+The system must not invent a default PAPER profile or silently copy a profile
+from another account. Until an explicit versioned default policy is approved,
+PAPER provisioning must either require explicit setup or remain unavailable for
+trading.
+
+Missing or invalid policy fails closed.
+
+## 10. Risk Facts Boundary
+
+The logical Risk Facts boundary SHALL be neutral and mode-independent:
+
+```text
+RiskFacts boundary
+    +-- LIVE facts
+    +-- PAPER facts
+```
+
+The boundary represents factual snapshots, completeness, timestamps, and
+provenance. It does not evaluate policy or authorize execution.
+
+The existing `BrokerRiskFactsPort` may remain temporarily as a LIVE adapter or
+compatibility boundary. This ADR does not require a mechanical rename. The
+semantic target is a neutral Risk Facts contract, not a naming-only refactor.
+
+## 11. Risk Facts Routing
+
+Risk Facts source selection belongs to Trading Core application orchestration
+or a mode-aware application adapter/router.
+
+The target flow is:
+
+```text
+Application layer
+    -> resolve financial Account
+    -> resolve canonical BrokerAccount
+    -> read execution mode
+    -> select authoritative facts source
+    -> assemble immutable RiskEvaluationContext
+    -> invoke Risk Domain
+```
+
+The Risk Domain SHALL NOT inspect:
+
+- `ExecutionMode`;
+- `BrokerProvider`;
+- repositories;
+- Feign clients;
+- provider DTOs;
+- Broker Service availability.
+
+Mode changes fact acquisition authority, not risk interpretation authority.
+
+## 12. LIVE Risk Facts
+
+LIVE financial and position facts remain externally authoritative where the
+provider owns them:
+
+```text
+LIVE
+    -> Broker Service
+    -> external provider
+    -> provider-neutral Risk Facts
+    -> immutable RiskEvaluationContext
+    -> Risk Domain
+```
+
+Local Trading Core projections may support display, audit, or correlation, but
+must not silently replace fresh provider authority for LIVE risk evaluation.
+
+This preserves ADR-042 and ADR-040 provider reconciliation semantics.
+
+## 13. PAPER Risk Facts
+
+PAPER facts are authoritative in Trading Core:
+
+```text
+PAPER
+    -> persisted Account / AccountBalance
+    -> persisted Trade and execution/fill state
+    -> local baseline and realized state where required
+    -> Market Data for current valuation inputs
+    -> provider-neutral Risk Facts
+```
+
+PAPER risk evaluation SHALL NOT require:
+
+- Broker Service account facts;
+- provider credentials;
+- provider balances;
+- provider position queries;
+- provider reconciliation;
+- external broker mutation.
+
+Market Data supplies current prices and conversion/valuation inputs only. It
+does not own PAPER account identity, balances, positions, or risk policy.
+
+## 14. Required Risk Facts
+
+The current Risk Domain consumes factual inputs including:
+
+- balance;
+- equity;
+- used and free margin;
+- daily-start balance;
+- daily closed PnL;
+- open positions;
+- position market value;
+- position loss at stop;
+- position margin;
+- current market prices;
+- proposed notional and expected loss;
+- required margin.
+
+Evidence:
+
+- `risk-domain/src/main/java/com/hope/trading/risk/snapshot/AccountSnapshot.java:8-27`
+- `risk-domain/src/main/java/com/hope/trading/risk/snapshot/PositionSnapshot.java:8-22`
+- `risk-domain/src/main/java/com/hope/trading/risk/metric/ObservedMetricsCalculator.java:6-12`
+- `risk-domain/src/main/java/com/hope/trading/risk/metric/ProjectionEngine.java:14-38`
+- `trading-core/src/main/java/com/hope/trading/trading_core/risk/application/TradePlanRiskEvaluationService.java:154-200`
+
+The authority matrix is:
+
+| Fact | LIVE authority | PAPER authority | Market Data required? |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Balances | Broker Service/provider | Local AccountBalance | No |
+| Equity | Provider facts plus valuation | Local state plus valuation | Often |
+| Used margin | Provider facts | Explicit supported PAPER calculation | As defined by calculation |
+| Daily start balance | Provider ledger/baseline | Local baseline or local ledger | Possibly |
+| Daily closed PnL | Provider trades/ledger | Local closed Trade/execution state | For conversion only |
+| Open exposure | Provider positions | Local OPEN Trade state | No |
+| Entry basis | Provider position | Local Trade/fill state | No |
+| Position value | Provider state plus valuation | Local exposure plus valuation | Yes |
+| Position risk/protection | Provider protective facts | Explicit local PAPER representation | Possibly |
+| Current price | Provider/market snapshot | Market Data | Yes |
+| Required margin | Broker-neutral authoritative source | Explicit supported PAPER source | Usually |
+| Provider position reference | Provider | Not applicable | No |
+
+The ADR does not invent PAPER margin, fee, slippage, or protective-stop
+semantics. Those remain implementation dependencies or separate decisions.
+
+## 15. Required Margin Gap
+
+The current required-margin implementation is deliberately unavailable:
+
+- `UnavailableRequiredMarginClient.java:7-13`
+
+It returns an empty result until an authoritative broker-neutral margin read
+exists. This can independently prevent complete T0/T1 evaluation.
+
+The required behavior is:
+
+```text
+missing required margin
+    -> risk context unavailable
+    -> no authorization
+```
+
+It must not become zero by default. Margin architecture is an implementation
+dependency and is not expanded by this ADR.
+
+## 16. T0 Identity Flow
+
+T0 SHALL use the financial Account identity:
+
+```text
+RiskEvaluation.Command.accountId
+    -> Account.accountId
+    -> Account ownership validation
+    -> canonical BrokerAccount relation
+    -> provider/mode validation
+    -> mode-aware Risk Facts source
+    -> immutable RiskEvaluationContext
+    -> Risk Domain
+```
+
+The risk configuration and assigned profile are keyed by the same financial
+Account ID. The linked BrokerAccount ID is used for routing and external facts,
+not as a substitute Account ID.
+
+## 17. T1 Identity Flow
+
+T1 SHALL resolve the same financial Account as T0.
+
+The target flow is:
+
+```text
+ExecutionIntent
+    + brokerAccountId
+    |     = routing identity
+    |
+    + TradePlanReference
+          -> TradePlan.tradingAccountId
+                = financial Account identity
+          -> Account
+          -> canonical BrokerAccount relation
+          -> relation must match intent.brokerAccountId
+          -> mode-aware Risk Facts source
+          -> T1 RiskEvaluationContext
+```
+
+The current behavior is incorrect:
+
+```text
+intent.brokerAccountId
+    -> AccountRepository.findById
+```
+
+The T1 risk persistence record must store the financial Account ID in its
+`account_id` field. Unavailable/error persistence must not substitute the
+BrokerAccount ID where the financial Account ID is known.
+
+## 18. Settlement Identity Consequence
+
+PAPER settlement must eventually resolve the same canonical financial Account
+used by T0 and T1:
+
+```text
+ExecutionIntent.brokerAccountId
+    -> canonical Account relation
+    -> Account financial state
+```
+
+`(owner, provider)` lookup is not an authoritative settlement mapping.
+
+Settlement implementation remains governed by ADR-042 and is not changed by
+this documentation ADR.
+
+## 19. Fail-Closed Behavior
+
+Required facts and configuration are mandatory inputs. The following conditions
+must prevent authorization:
+
+- financial Account missing;
+- canonical relation missing;
+- linked ownership inconsistent;
+- provider or execution mode inconsistent;
+- RiskConfiguration missing;
+- assigned RiskProfile missing;
+- RiskProfile invalid or incomplete;
+- required Market Data unavailable or incomplete;
+- required margin unavailable;
+- local PAPER state inconsistent;
+- required valuation impossible.
+
+Failures must remain distinguishable where practical:
+
+| Condition | Classification |
+|---|---|
+| Missing Account | Account/domain lookup failure |
+| Missing relation or inconsistent owner | Mapping/domain invariant failure |
+| Missing configuration/profile | Configuration unavailable |
+| Invalid profile | Configuration invalid |
+| Missing market input | Valuation unavailable |
+| Missing margin | Risk dependency unavailable |
+| Inconsistent local state | Domain/context invalid |
+
+No missing fact may silently become zero, empty exposure, unlimited risk, or a
+successful validation unless that value is proven authoritative.
+
+## 20. Security and Ownership
+
+Authorization must follow the complete identity chain:
+
+```text
+authenticated user
+    -> BrokerAccount.ownerId
+    -> linked Account.user.userId
+    -> Account financial state
+    -> risk configuration/profile
+    -> local PAPER positions
+```
+
+The application must validate ownership before exposing or mutating either
+account's state. A database relation alone is insufficient if it permits
+cross-user links.
+
+Provider and execution mode must be validated from the linked BrokerAccount,
+not accepted from an untrusted client as authoritative facts.
+
+## 21. Migration and Legacy Data
+
+This ADR introduces no migration. Future implementation requires:
+
+```text
+SCHEMA_CHANGE_REQUIRED = YES
+BACKFILL_REQUIRED = YES
+BACKFILL_DETERMINISTIC_FOR_ALL_ROWS = NO
+AMBIGUOUS_LEGACY_ROWS_POSSIBLE = YES
+```
+
+Provable backfill evidence may include:
+
+- existing `account_risk_configuration.broker_account_id`;
+- valid Account and BrokerAccount existence;
+- matching ownership;
+- matching provider;
+- consistent execution mode.
+
+`(owner, provider)` is not sufficient as a universal backfill key. Existing
+BrokerAccount rows can have the same owner/provider, while the Account model's
+`UNIQUE(user_id, broker)` constraint represents a different and narrower rule.
+
+The Story 0038 equal-UUID fixture is not migration evidence.
+
+Future migration must:
+
+- backfill only provable mappings;
+- quarantine or reject ambiguous rows;
+- require explicit manual resolution where necessary;
+- never choose the first matching account;
+- never reinterpret existing UUID meaning;
+- preserve existing LIVE external authority.
+
+## 22. Database Constraint Direction
+
+Future schema work should distinguish:
+
+### Database-enforceable invariants
+
+- foreign key from the canonical relation to `broker_account`;
+- first-milestone uniqueness for the one-to-one relationship;
+- required relation after a complete migration/provisioning transition;
+- existence of the linked Account and BrokerAccount.
+
+### Domain/application invariants
+
+- Account owner equals BrokerAccount owner;
+- provider metadata consistency;
+- execution-mode lifecycle validity;
+- risk readiness;
+- mode-correct fact routing;
+- complete and trustworthy local PAPER facts.
+
+The existing `UNIQUE(user_id, broker)` constraint must be explicitly reviewed
+and safely replaced or relaxed during implementation if multiple accounts for a
+provider are supported. It is not changed by this ADR.
+
+## 23. Alternatives Considered: Identity
+
+### A. Same Account/BrokerAccount UUID
+
+Rejected.
+
+- the entities have different responsibilities;
+- production creates independent identifiers;
+- equality hides incorrect lookups;
+- it couples financial identity to execution routing;
+- Story 0038 demonstrates the resulting false confidence.
+
+### B. Explicit durable relation
+
+Accepted.
+
+- explicit and auditable;
+- deterministic;
+- supports multiple accounts;
+- preserves distinct identities;
+- allows ownership/provider/mode invariants to be validated.
+
+### C. `(owner, provider)` lookup
+
+Rejected as canonical identity.
+
+- ambiguous with multiple accounts;
+- does not identify a financial Account;
+- current Account and BrokerAccount uniqueness rules differ;
+- cannot safely support LIVE/PAPER coexistence.
+
+### D. Dedicated identity entity or value object
+
+Deferred.
+
+The first milestone does not justify another abstraction if an explicit one-to-
+one relation is sufficient. A future identity abstraction may be introduced if
+the relationship becomes more complex than the current model supports.
+
+## 24. Alternatives Considered: Risk Facts
+
+### A. Use `BrokerRiskFactsPort` for every mode
+
+Rejected as the long-term semantic boundary.
+
+It gives Broker Service/provider facts authority over PAPER state and requires
+credentials or an external account that PAPER does not possess.
+
+### B. Neutral mode-aware Risk Facts boundary
+
+Accepted.
+
+It preserves the distinction between factual inputs and risk interpretation and
+supports both external LIVE facts and local PAPER facts.
+
+### C. Router above the existing LIVE adapter
+
+Accepted as a staged implementation technique.
+
+The existing LIVE adapter can remain while a mode-aware router selects a local
+PAPER source.
+
+### D. Mode branching inside the Risk Domain
+
+Rejected.
+
+It would make the deterministic Risk Domain aware of infrastructure and
+execution providers. Mode belongs to fact acquisition, not rule interpretation.
